_what: The Barrows chest as Old School documents it, so the battery has something to compare the scripts AGAINST rather than comparing them with themselves.

_quotes.rolls: There is initially one roll at the drop table. Each additional brother killed grants an additional roll at the drop table, to a maximum of seven total rolls.
_quotes.equipment: In order to receive a piece of Barrows equipment, the corresponding brother must be killed before the chest is looted.
_quotes.roll: A roll is performed for a value between 1 and your reward potential (each inclusive). The result then determines what item is awarded, and in what quantity.
_quotes.potential: The reward potential gathered is equal to the combat level of the monster that was slain, capped for a total of 1,000. For every Barrows brother that was slain, the player will receive an extra 2 points on their rewards potential, capping the maximum reward potential at 1,012.
_quotes.doors: Upon opening any of the doors in these tunnels, a monster will spawn and attack the player. When opening a door to a room that already contains eleven enemies or more, no new monster will be spawned.
_quotes.afterloot: Each door you open is guaranteed to summon one of the brothers whom you did not kill.

equipment._note: P(N) = 1/(450 - 58*N) per roll, N = brothers killed: 1/392 at one brother and 1/102 at six.

_table_note: The rp column is the reward potential an item needs before it can be rolled at all, and it is also the band: the roll is a value in 1..potential, and the item awarded is the last one in this list whose rp the roll reached. The bands therefore run 1-380 coins, 381-505 mind, 506-630 chaos, 631-755 death, 756-880 blood, 881-1005 bolt rack, 1006-1011 key half, 1012 dragon med helm - 380 + 125*5 + 6 + 1 = 1012 exactly. The wiki's own rates column prints coins as 379/1012, one short of the band its thresholds describe; the thresholds are what is implemented, because they are the side that adds up.
_monsters_note: Combat levels read off the npc records in scripts/_unpack/377/all.npc, not off the wiki: these are 377's own Barrows monsters and the battery re-reads them from the same place the engine does.

teleport._note: Corey's addition, not Old School's: the chest pays a Barrows teleport at 1/10 on a looted chest, four to six of them. The destination is the tile he asked for.
